item.title: Trump Gives Putin an ‘Economic Lifeline,’ Waives Sanctions on Russia. “These waivers have nothing to do with our national security, and everything to do with sucking up to Vladimir Putin,” said US Sen. Richard Blumenthal.
item.description: President Donald Trump on Friday signed an executive order that waived new sanctions on Russia that were set to take effect thanks to bipartisan legislation signed into law by the president last month. Trump justified the decision by claiming the sanctions waiver “is in the national interests of the United States,” without offering further details. The president said he submitted a report to Congress elaborating on his reasons for waiving the sanctions. A Friday report in The New York Times described the waiver as “another economic lifeline to Russian President Vladimir V. Putin,” as the sanctions had been designed “to target Russian officials, oligarchs, and financial institutions” and “squeeze the financial lifelines sustaining Russia’s war against Ukraine.” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the sanctions waiver, and urged US lawmakers and voters to speak out against the US president’s actions. “It is important that everyone in America... sees what is really happening,” Zelenskyy wrote in a Saturday social media post. “At a time when the Russians have carried out such a massive attack on our energy sector, a decision was unfortunately made in America to completely disregard the [sanctions law], which was supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end.” Zelenskyy emphasized that the sanctions package could still do a lot of good, but “it needs to actually work, and every voice in support of it matters.”

item.title: Body Swap
item.description:
We want to remember the good internet. The cat clips, the funny family tales, the great comic feats. The internet that makes us laugh. That's the internet we grew up on and the the one we want want to be a part of. We know that the world wide web is not always a great place. Its like we are full of contradictions. One moment you're laughing at a tortoise enjoying a fresh lettuce leaf, the next you stumble across some heinous hateful trash. Thats what it feels like to be online today. Your brain cannot stand this whiplash. Sometimes we want to throw our phones into the river and be done with it all. But then we remember you, our readers. And the good internet. And that its not time to give up just yet. If you want to support our work, here's the link: https://www.patreon.com/warandpeas
If you’ve been reading our comics for a while, you’ll know that we’re a bunch of tree-huggin’ saps. We love using our silly talents to spread our appreciation of Mother Nature. Comics have thus far been our favorite medium to do so. But a few years ago, an idea started brewing in our minds: what if we left the world of drawing and make-believe and created something out there, a real place with real trees. And thus an idea grew: let’s plant a forest.
And what kind of forest would we want to build? A FUNNY FOREST of course. And we’re building it with the help of you and our community on Patreon. Everybody told us this idea was crazy. Everybody except the Naturlandstiftung Saar, who said, “Sure, we’ll help you build a funny forest” – which is good news for the trees because they plant trees for a living. But we still need help and that’s where you come in. If you want us to plant a tree for you, listen up:
- You’re already a patron? You get a tree! - You’re not a patron yet? Sign up and you get a tree. - The deadline to sign up is November 30th, 2026 (because at some point we have to tell the tree people a number) - You want to plant it yourself? Come to our planting party. If you can’t make it, we’ll plant it for you. - Where is the planting party? On the Peterberg in beautiful Nonnweiler, Saarland, Germany. - When is it? Early December, we hope. The exact date depends on the weather but we will let you know in time. Join the party here: https://www.patreon.com/warandpeas Let’s plant a freaking forest! Forever yours, Elizabeth and Jonathan

item.description: Mark Cuban asked a question back in January that every American with health insurance should be asking. Why would an insurance company pay $2,500 for an MRI when a center down the street will do it for $350? The replies filled up with people who had lived it. One person was quoted more than $1,500 through insurance and paid $275 cash at an independent imaging center. Another was quoted $1,200 to $3,200 through insurance and found the same scan for $212. Others shared insurance bills from about $2,400 to more than $9,000 for scans they could have gotten for a few hundred dollars somewhere else. Most of the gap comes down to where you get the scan. Hospitals set their own prices, and those prices often have very little to do with what the MRI costs to perform. Independent imaging centers usually charge a fraction of that for the same scan on similar equipment. Cuban said hospitals will even raise the bill when they think an insurer is willing to pay more, and he called healthcare a game of who can rip off who. Some people pushed back that insurers don't set prices and simply pay what providers bill. Either way, the patient and the employer end up covering the difference through higher premiums and bigger out-of-pocket bills. This is the same Mark Cuban behind Cost Plus Drugs, which sells medications at cost plus a small, published markup. So before your next MRI, CT scan, or X-ray, make two calls. Call an independent imaging center and ask for the cash price. Then call your insurance company and ask which independent centers near you are in-network, because that scan can be just as cheap and still count toward your deductible. That second part matters more than people realize. Cash payments usually don't count toward your deductible or out-of-pocket max, so if you're likely to hit your max this year because of a surgery or ongoing treatment, using insurance can still be the smarter move. If you pay cash, ask for a written good faith estimate, which self-pay patients are entitled to by law. A couple of phone calls can easily save you a thousand dollars or more on a single scan.

item.description: Donald Trump told a Kentucky crowd Saturday that “if the Republicans win,” the Department of War will put $100 million into a Winchester drug plant. The Pentagon didn’t answer questions about the pledge, and the governor’s office said it had no information. In the same speech Trump again promised $5,000 checks to every adult if Republicans keep Congress. He has been promising to pay Americans for weeks, $500 to some on Obamacare and $90 to some seniors. The House impeached him in 2019 for holding up $391 million in military aid while he asked Ukraine’s president to “do us a favor.” This time the favor is your vote, and he’s offering your own money for it.
